description: The linear algebra that data science and machine learning run on: vectors and vector spaces, matrices and their operations, solving linear systems, determinants and inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonality, projections and least squares, and the singular value decomposition behind principal component analysis. Each idea is seen geometrically in interactive browser plots, worked by hand, and then implemented in NumPy on real data.
modelledOn: Lay, Lay and McDonald, Linear Algebra and Its Applications
Boyd and Vandenberghe, Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra: Vectors, Matrices, and Least Squares
Deisenroth, Faisal and Ong, Mathematics for Machine Learning (linear algebra chapters)
outcomes: Represent data as vectors and matrices and reason about linear combinations, span, independence, basis and dimension.
Solve linear systems by Gaussian elimination and LU factorisation and interpret their solutions through the four fundamental subspaces.
Compute determinants and inverses and explain when a matrix is invertible and how conditioning affects numerical results.
Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalise matrices and apply them to dynamical systems and Markov chains.
Use orthogonality, projections, QR factorisation and least squares to fit models to data.
Derive and apply the singular value decomposition for low-rank approximation and principal component analysis.

units.title: Vectors
topics: Vectors as arrows, as lists of numbers and as data points; feature vectors for customers, images and documents
Vector addition, scalar multiplication and linear combinations; geometric interpretation in 2D and 3D
Dot product, length, angle and cosine similarity; the Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities
Norms: L1, L2 and infinity norms; distance between data points
NumPy arrays, broadcasting and vectorised computation

units.title: Vector spaces
topics: Span, linear independence and dependence
Subspaces, basis and dimension; coordinates relative to a basis and change of basis
Column space, null space, row space and left null space; rank
The rank-nullity theorem and the four fundamental subspaces

units.title: Matrices and matrix operations
topics: Matrices as data tables and as linear transformations; rotation, scaling, shear and projection in the plane
Matrix-vector and matrix-matrix multiplication: row, column and outer-product views
Transpose, symmetric matrices, identity, diagonal, triangular and permutation matrices
Block matrices and the cost of matrix computations
Adjacency matrices of graphs: a road network between market towns

units.title: Systems of linear equations
topics: Linear systems in matrix form; the row picture and the column picture
Gaussian elimination, row echelon and reduced row echelon form; pivots and free variables
Existence and uniqueness: consistent, inconsistent and underdetermined systems
LU factorisation and solving many right-hand sides; partial pivoting
Numerical issues: floating-point error, ill-conditioning and the condition number
Applications: balancing a mixing problem for animal feed and network flow

units.title: Determinants and inverses
topics: The inverse matrix: definition, Gauss-Jordan computation and the invertible matrix theorem
Determinants: cofactor expansion, row operations and properties
The determinant as signed volume and as a test for invertibility
Cramer's rule in brief; why software solves systems instead of inverting matrices

units.title: Orthogonality and projections
topics: Orthogonal vectors and subspaces; orthogonal complements
Projection onto a line and onto a subspace; projection matrices
Least squares: the normal equations and fitting a line or plane to data
Orthonormal bases, the Gram-Schmidt process and QR factorisation
Orthogonal matrices and their numerical stability
Fitting a trend to maize prices in Kumasi by least squares

units.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; the characteristic polynomial; geometric meaning
Diagonalisation, powers of a matrix and repeated linear maps
Symmetric matrices and the spectral theorem; positive definite matrices and quadratic forms
Markov chains and steady states; PageRank as an eigenvector problem
The power method and how libraries compute eigenvalues
Covariance matrices and their eigenvectors as directions of variation

units.title: Singular value decomposition and PCA
topics: The singular value decomposition: existence, geometry and relation to eigen-decomposition
Low-rank approximation and the Eckart-Young theorem; image compression with the SVD
Pseudoinverse and minimum-norm least squares
Principal component analysis derived from the SVD: centring, explained variance and scree plots
Applications: recommender systems by matrix factorisation and latent semantic analysis of text
Capstone: reducing and visualising a multi-indicator dataset of Ghanaian districts with PCA

schedule.title: Vectors, dot products and similarity
schedule.exercise: Represent three customers as feature vectors, compute their pairwise cosine similarities by hand and say which two are most alike and why.

tasks.title: Plot two 2D vectors, their sum and a linear combination 2a minus b on the same axes, and read off the coordinates
Compute dot products and angles for six pairs of vectors and verify the Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities on each pair
Turn five short documents into word-count vectors, rank them by cosine similarity to a query, and explain a ranking that looks wrong

schedule.title: Norms and NumPy
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page explanation of when to prefer the L1 norm over the L2 norm for measuring distance between data points.

tasks.title: Compute L1, L2 and infinity norms of four vectors and draw the unit ball for each norm in the plane
Use NumPy broadcasting to compute all pairwise distances among 100 points without loops, and check three entries by hand
Compare nearest neighbours of a query point under L1, L2 and infinity distances on a small data set and explain why the answers differ

schedule.title: Span, bases and subspaces
schedule.exercise: Decide by hand whether four given vectors in R3 are independent, and describe the subspace they span in words.

tasks.title: Test whether three given vectors are linearly independent by row reduction and state the dimension of their span
Find the coordinates of a vector relative to a new basis and use the change-of-basis matrix to convert back and forth
Find bases for the four fundamental subspaces of a 4 by 5 matrix and verify rank-nullity and the orthogonality of the subspaces

schedule.title: Matrices as transformations
schedule.exercise: Describe the effect of five given 2 by 2 matrices on the unit square and say which are invertible and why.

tasks.title: Apply rotation, scaling, shear and projection matrices to the unit square and plot each image
Multiply two matrices using the row, column and outer-product views, and check that all three views give the same product
Build the adjacency matrix of a road network between six market towns and use its powers to count routes of each length between towns

schedule.title: Solving linear systems
schedule.exercise: Solve a 3 by 3 system by hand with Gaussian elimination and describe its row picture and column picture.

tasks.title: Row reduce a 3 by 4 augmented matrix to reduced echelon form and read off the solution and any free variables
Classify six systems as one solution, no solution or infinitely many, and give the general solution where it exists
Find the intersection of three planes in each of the cases unique point, line and empty, and relate each to the rank of the matrix

schedule.title: Factorisation and numerical issues
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why an LU factorisation is cheaper than repeated elimination when the same matrix has many right-hand sides.

tasks.title: Compute an LU factorisation of a 3 by 3 matrix, then solve two different right-hand sides using the same factors
Solve a nearly singular system, compute its condition number, and show how a tiny change in the data moves the answer a lot
Set up and solve the linear system that mixes four feed ingredients to meet protein, fibre and cost targets, and test sensitivity to prices

schedule.title: Inverses and determinants
schedule.exercise: Prove that a matrix with a zero determinant has dependent columns, and give a 3 by 3 example.

tasks.title: Find the inverse of a 3 by 3 matrix by Gauss-Jordan elimination and verify that the product with the original is the identity
Compute a determinant by cofactor expansion and by row operations and check that both methods agree on four matrices
Time solving a 500 by 500 system by direct inversion and by a factorisation solver, and compare accuracy and speed

schedule.title: Orthogonality and least squares
schedule.exercise: Derive the normal equations from minimising the squared error for a straight line, and check the result on four data points by hand.

tasks.title: Check orthogonality of vector pairs and compute the orthogonal complement of a line in the plane
Project a vector onto a subspace using a projection matrix and verify that the error is orthogonal to the subspace
Fit a plane to 30 noisy points by the normal equations, plot the residuals and explain what a large residual says about the data

schedule.title: Orthonormal bases and trend fitting
schedule.exercise: Describe why Gram-Schmidt applied to nearly parallel vectors loses accuracy, and suggest the remedy.

tasks.title: Apply Gram-Schmidt to three vectors in R3 and verify that the resulting vectors are orthonormal
Compute a QR factorisation and use it to solve a least squares problem, comparing the answer with the normal equations
Fit linear and quadratic trends to monthly maize prices in Kumasi by least squares, compare residuals, and forecast the next three months with a caution

schedule.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
schedule.exercise: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 2 by 2 matrix by hand and describe in words what the matrix does along each eigenvector.

tasks.title: Compute the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 2 by 2 matrix and plot the vectors that stay on their line
Diagonalise a 3 by 3 matrix and use the diagonal form to compute its tenth power, verifying against repeated multiplication
Use the spectral theorem on a symmetric matrix to classify a quadratic form as positive definite, then plot its level curves

schedule.title: Markov chains and variation
schedule.exercise: Describe the PageRank idea for a five-page web in your own words, including what the damping factor is for.

tasks.title: Find the steady state of a two-state weather Markov chain by solving for the eigenvector with eigenvalue one
Implement the power method to find the dominant eigenvalue of a matrix, and chart how fast it converges for different eigenvalue gaps
Compute the covariance matrix of a 3-feature data set, find its eigenvectors, and interpret the direction of greatest variation

schedule.title: The singular value decomposition
schedule.exercise: Explain the geometry of the SVD of a 2 by 2 matrix as a rotation, a stretch and another rotation, with a sketch.

tasks.title: Compute the SVD of a small matrix and verify the three factors multiply back to the original
Compress a grayscale image with the SVD at ranks 5, 20 and 50 and report the storage and error for each
Compute the pseudoinverse of a rank-deficient matrix from its SVD and use it to find the minimum-norm least squares solution

schedule.title: PCA and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: explain the variables, how you centred and scaled them, how many components you kept and what each component means for Ghanaian districts.

tasks.title: Run PCA on a small data set by the SVD and draw a scree plot of explained variance for each component
Factorise a small ratings matrix into user and item factors and predict three missing ratings, checking the error on held-out entries
Reduce a multi-indicator data set of Ghanaian districts to two principal components, plot the districts, and interpret the clusters and outliers
